title: The Greatness of Those Who Renounce
note: This chapter tells the greatness of sages who have renounced completely. They are the ones who show the world righteousness and the rest as they truly are, so it follows the greatness of rain.

couplets.plain: The settled view of the books is that the greatness of those who renounce while holding to right conduct stands above all else.
couplets.pm: The books settle that, of all excellent things, the greatness of those who renounce while keeping their own conduct is highest. Keeping the conduct of your varna and stage of life grows righteousness, wears down sin and ends ignorance. Longing for release, yoga and true knowledge follow, and “mine” and “I” fall away. Even religious books that disagree agree on this.

links.quote: those who renounce while holding to right conduct
links.reason: Speaks of those who renounce while holding to right conduct.
The books put the greatness of those who renounce above all else.

couplets.plain: Trying to measure the greatness of those who renounce is like counting all who have died on earth.
couplets.pm: To state in a number the greatness of those who have let go of both kinds of attachment is like trying to count all who have been born in this world and died. It can’t be done.

links.quote: the greatness of those who renounce
links.reason: Those who renounce are named outright and declared beyond all counting.

links.quote: like counting all who have died on earth

couplets.plain: The greatness of those who have weighed the two and taken up righteousness here shines out in the world.
couplets.pm: Only the greatness of those who have examined birth and release, the sorrow of one and the joy of the other, and taken up the righteousness of renunciation here to end birth, stands high in the world. “Only” sets it above the greatness of emperors who ruled the whole earth. These three couplets say the greatness of those who renounce exceeds all other greatness.
couplets.note: “The two” is all the Tamil says. He takes them as birth and release, and the righteousness as renunciation.

links.quote: those who have weighed the two
links.reason: These are people who made their choice after weighing the two.
The greatness of those who chose this path is what shines out in the world.

couplets.plain: Whoever guards the five senses with the goad called firmness is a seed for the land called the highest.
couplets.pm: Whoever uses the goad of firmness to hold the five elephants of the senses back from their objects is a seed for the land of release, called the highest of all lands. Firmness here means knowledge. He is called a seed because he sprouts in that land: he isn’t someone who is born here and dies and comes back.

links.reason: Praises the firmness that drives the five senses as a goad drives a beast.
The goad is an elephant’s hook, so the five senses are driven like elephants and firmness steers them.

links.quote: a seed for the land called the highest
links.reason: Such a person is a seed that will come up in the land called the highest.

couplets.plain: Of the strength of one who quenched the five senses, Indra himself, ruler of those in the wide sky, is witness enough.
couplets.pm: Indra, ruler of those in the wide sky, is witness enough to the strength of one who has held down all five desires. He didn’t quench them himself and fell under a curse, and that shows the strength of one who did.

links.quote: the strength of one who quenched the five senses
links.reason: Calls Indra as witness to the strength of one who has quenched the five senses.

couplets.plain: Those who do what is hard to do are great. Those who can’t are small.
couplets.pm: Among people of equal birth, those who leave what is easy and do what is hard are great. Those who do the easy and can’t do the hard are small. The easy is letting the mind run to sense objects, with greed and anger. The hard is the eight limbs of yoga. He rejects taking it as ascetic feats like bathing often, which fall within one limb and don’t suit this greatness.

links.quote: Those who do what is hard to do are great
links.reason: Draws the line between the great and the small at doing what is hard to do.

couplets.plain: The world lies with the one who knows the workings of the five: taste, light, touch, sound and smell.
couplets.pm: The world lies within the understanding of one who examines the divisions of these five subtle elements. With the gross elements and the organs of sense and action they make twenty. The self, intellect, ego, mind and root nature make twenty-five, as Samkhya teaches. No world exists apart from these. The causes of greatness are quenching the five, yoga and true knowledge.

couplets.plain: The hidden words of people whose speech comes true show their greatness on earth.
couplets.pm: The mantras they speak as commands show, before your eyes, the greatness on earth of those who have renounced, whose words are full. A full word gives its result whether spoken in compassion or in anger. To show here means to make known through the result.

links.reason: Those whose speech comes true are, in this chapter, those who renounce.

couplets.plain: The anger of those who stand on the hill called virtue is hard to withstand, even for a moment.
couplets.pm: The anger of ascetics who stand at the top of the hill of good qualities, such as renunciation, true knowledge and freedom from craving, is hard for its target to stop, even for the instant it lasts. Qualities are a hill because they are firm and great. Old habit may raise anger, but true knowledge destroys it at once. It can’t be stopped because their word is full.

links.quote: The anger of those who stand on the hill called virtue
links.reason: Warns that the anger of those on the hill of virtue is hard to withstand, even for a moment.
Virtue is a hill that they have climbed and stand on.

couplets.plain: Those called sages are the righteous, because they live with tenderness towards every living thing.
couplets.pm: Those called sages are those in the righteousness of renunciation, because they take a vow of fine tenderness towards all living beings. The name means people of lovely coolness, so it applies only to those with such compassion. Though they have the power of command, they have compassion for all beings.

links.reason: Takes the title of sage and gives it to those who have earned it by tenderness.
Makes tenderness towards all life the reason anyone deserves the name.
